route: 6 (keying polarity) + 5 (subscale block) + 1/7 (published loading, marker item) + 3 (published subscale norms, option axis)
evidence: Live table (irw_fetch, n=203 per item, 31 items) -- see verify_gomez_2022_qcae.R. 27 of 31 items are tied to text by the source .sav's numbered variable labels and the IRW code IS the .sav column name, so only the four unlabelled reverse-recoded columns needed checking. (a) Keying polarity: item-rest r = +0.542 (QCAE1r, OS), +0.568 (QCAE2r, PER), +0.219 (QCAE17r, PER), +0.609 (QCAE29r, PER) -- all positive, so all four are stored already reverse-scored and their shipped anchors are flipped. (b) Subscale block: QCAE1r vs OS-rest r = +0.542 vs PER r = +0.172, so QCAE1r is the single reverse-worded Online Simulation item. (c) Marker/published loading: the paper reports .29 for item 17 and .36 for item 31, the only two sub-.40 loadings; observed, QCAE17r is the weakest PER item (+0.219 vs +0.521..+0.609) and correlates only +0.183/+0.145/+0.221 with the three narrative PER items, while QCAE31 is the weakest OS item (+0.334 vs next-lowest +0.519) -- consistent with Queiros et al. (2018), who print item 17's wording by number and say items 2, 11, 29 are the narrative ones. (d) option_text<->resp direction: summed as stored, Cognitive Empathy M = 58.80 (SD 9.57) and Affective M = 34.57 (5.82) against published norms 57.14 (8.28)/33.75 (5.51) (Powell 2018, n=844) and 59.42/36.76 (Reniers 2011); the flipped reading gives 36.20 and 25.43, so the .sav value labels are right and the paper's Methods sentence ('1 (strongly agree) ... 4 (strongly disagree)') is an error. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: QCAE2r vs QCAE29r. Both are narrative-context PER items, item-rest +0.568 vs +0.609 and mutual r +0.573, and no published quantity is keyed to their text; the 2-vs-29 assignment rests on Reniers' documented item sourcing (IRI supplies items 1-6, the Empathy Quotient items 15-29), not on the data. Hence PARTIAL.

route: 8 (semantic coherence of the response distribution) + 5 (block structure in the correlation matrix)
evidence: Four content-derived predictions, all confirmed on live data (n=2,534-2,548 per item except AVOID2 n=847). (a) AVOID4 'avoid having romantic relationships' has the highest mean of the 11, 3.029, ahead of AVOID3 2.987 and AVOID2 2.991. (b) The two lowest are AVOID8 'working with each other' 2.341 and AVOID6 'shopping in stores' 2.351 -- the two structurally least-avoidable domains -- against 2.534-3.029 for the rest. (c) The largest off-diagonal correlation in the 11x11 matrix is r(AVOID10,AVOID11)=0.896, matching appendix positions 10 and 11, which are near-synonymous ('if they had a choice, they would rather not interact' / 'if they can avoid interacting, they do'). (d) Of all 165 item triples, the tightest is {AVOID9,AVOID10,AVOID11} at mean within-triple r=0.854, and the second tightest is {AVOID1,AVOID2,AVOID3} at 0.828 (next best 0.816) -- i.e. the top two of 165 are exactly the appendix's general 'if ... interact' triple and its informal-social-contact triple. This pins the block structure, the ends of the mean ordering and the 10/11 pair. It does NOT separate positions 1/2/3 from one another (means 2.922/2.991/2.987, mutually r=0.80-0.86), nor 5 from 7, so PARTIAL rather than VERIFIED.

route: 8 (semantic coherence) + near-synonym adjacency in the correlation matrix
evidence: Route 8 (semantic coherence of the response distribution) + a near-synonym adjacency check on the correlation matrix; live data via irw_fetch (21,167 rows, 9 items). (A) Per-item means on the 1 = never .. 7 = frequently scale: DISCRIM1 3.71, D2 3.70, D3 3.49, D4 3.53, D5 3.59, D6 3.83, D7 3.65, D8 3.16, D9 3.04. The two lowest are exactly DISCRIM8 and DISCRIM9, the appendix's two overt-harassment items ('Being called names or insulted', 'Being threatened or harassed'), with D9 <= D8 (3.04 vs 3.16) as the more extreme event should be; every EDS administration puts those two at the bottom, so a permutation moving either into the middle is ruled out. (B) The appendix order contains exactly two near-synonym pairs, (1 courtesy, 2 respect) and (8 names, 9 threatened), and they are the two strongest of the 36 correlations: r(D1,D2) = 0.907 and r(D8,D9) = 0.863, against a next-highest 0.822 (D2,D3) and 0.816 (D6,D7). Re-run on Study 1 alone (n = 847, the only sample complete on all nine items, since DISCRIM2's Study-2 column was dropped as a spreadsheet artifact): 0.907 and 0.887 against 0.837 next. NOT ESTABLISHED: this does not separate DISCRIM3, DISCRIM4 and DISCRIM5 (poorer service / not smart / afraid of him-her; means 3.49, 3.53, 3.59, no near-synonym among them) from one another, and it does not tell DISCRIM1 from DISCRIM2 within their pair (3.71 vs 3.70) -- it pins the pair to positions 1-2, not the order inside it. Hence PARTIAL.
